title: Decide an SMT-LIB script with z3
when: checking whether a goal over integers, reals and uninterpreted functions follows from hypotheses, by refuting its negation
getting an unsat core: the hypotheses a proof needs, to hand to grind, aesop or hammer
whenNot: proving the theorem: unsat is evidence that Lean has not checked, and only a Lean proof settles a claim
goals outside the fragment (sets, sums, casts): translate what you can, or use the Lean battery

smtlib.description: An SMT-LIB 2 script ending with (check-sat); with (set-option :produce-unsat-cores true), (assert (! F :named n)) and (get-unsat-core) the answer carries the core

timeoutSec.description: z3's time limit in seconds, 30 when not given

model.description: Print the model when the answer is sat

status.description: Read from the first line of z3's output, never from its prose

core.description: For unsat: the names of the assertions in the unsat core

input.smtlib:
(set-option :produce-unsat-cores true)
(declare-const x Int)
(assert (! (> x 0) :named a))
(assert (! (< x 0) :named b))
(check-sat)
(get-unsat-core)

implementations.description: z3 as a process (`z3 -in -smt2 -T:N`, the script on standard input), from PyPI's z3-solver or the system's z3. The command is a setting (Z3_COMMAND).
